clue.text: Reckon American tree will be found by river

parts.note: the fig is a fruit tree
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A pondering American wonders whether a tree grows beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American' belongs to the definition: 'I figure' for 'I reckon' is chiefly US usage. 'will be found by' just places the tree beside the river.
explanation.definitionFit: In American speech to suppose or calculate something is to figure it, as in 'I figure he's late'.

clue.text: This combined with swindle would become muddled

indicators.note: the clue says this word plus a swindle would make the word for muddled, so the swindle is taken away from that longer word

parts.note: muddled means confused
a con is a swindle

explanation.surface: Someone warns that mixing this with a swindle would leave everyone muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: CON put with the answer makes CONFUSED (muddled), so remove CON from CONFUSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Things fused are joined or melded together into one.

clue.text: Plant circular pieces in set

indicators.note: in places the circular pieces within the word for set

parts.note: to set, as jelly does, is to gel
rounds are circular pieces, slices of something

explanation.surface: A gardener's instruction to plant round cuttings in a set pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundsel is a common weed, a yellow-flowered member of the daisy family.

clue.text: River behind something floating on it?

parts.note: aft means behind, at the rear of a ship

explanation.surface: A river with something trailing behind, perhaps a craft floating on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' in the definition points back to the river in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A raft is a flat buoyant platform that drifts on water.

clue.text: Met to promote candidate — led to copper being taken on board

indicators.note: taken on board means carried inside, so the copper sits within the word for led to

parts.note: to cause is to lead to, so led to means caused
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Party members gathered to push a candidate, and a policeman was brought into the scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the element. 'led to' is past tense, matching the past-tense definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A caucus is a party meeting to choose candidates, so to have caucused is to have held such a meeting.

clue.text: Ways one part of the army set up its required collection?

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means written upwards, so both pieces are read backwards

parts.note: lanes are ways, roads
RA is the Royal Artillery, part of the British Army

explanation.surface: A soldier explains how one section of the army arranges its required kit.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'set up' reads the whole charade upwards. 'its' refers back to the army, whose required collection is its weapons store; 'one' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a store of weapons and ammunition, the stock an army must have.

clue.text: French mistress to speak English, one blocking narrow street

parts.note: to chat is to speak

indicators.note: blocking means standing in the way inside, so one sits within the narrow street

parts.note: a lane is a narrow street
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A French mistress chats in English while someone obstructs an alley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French mistress' is not a teacher: the word comes from the lady of a French chateau.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatelaine is the woman in charge of a large house or castle, from French chatelaine.

clue.text: American upset doctor, a low caste Hindu

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upwards, so the letters for American are read backwards

explanation.surface: An American got cross with a doctor of low social caste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns US to SU; the comma makes 'a' look like part of the definition, but it supplies the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sudras are the lowest of the four traditional Hindu varnas, labourers and servants.

clue.text: One may have roamed around in arid environment

definitions.text: One may have roamed around in arid environment

indicators.note: environment means surroundings, so the word for arid surrounds the shuffled letters

parts.note: arid means dry

indicators.note: around signals the letters of roamed are rearranged

explanation.surface: A camel is pictured wandering about a desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' shuffles the letters of 'roamed' and 'environment' wraps the arid word round them. Read as a whole, the clue also describes a desert camel, so it is an all-in-one.
explanation.definitionFit: The dromedary, the one-humped camel, lives in desert lands.

clue.text: A party's to have lots of sailors etc. Invading decks

indicators.note: invading means getting inside, so the sailors go into the party's

parts.note: a do is a party, and the 's adds S
RN is the Royal Navy, lots of sailors and ships

explanation.surface: A party has a crowd of sailors gatecrashing the ship's decks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decks' looks like a ship's floors, but it is a verb: to deck out.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck is to decorate or embellish, as in decking halls with holly.

clue.text: Was jeering as fare was dealt with?

explanation.surface: Someone mocked while food was eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is both to mock with jeers and, informally, to eat greedily, which deals with the food.

clue.text: Difficult person not too bad, joiner in

indicators.note: in places the joiner inside the phrase for not too bad

parts.note: so-so means middling, not too bad
and is a conjunction, a joining word

explanation.surface: A tricky carpenter is described as not too bad at his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joiner' looks like a carpenter but means a conjunction.
explanation.definitionFit: A so-and-so is a euphemism for an unpleasant or awkward individual.

clue.text: Poet said to be accomplished

indicators.note: said means spoken, so it is the sound of the poet's name that counts

parts.note: John Donne was an English metaphysical poet

explanation.surface: A poet is reputed to be skilful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accomplished' looks like 'skilled', but it means finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Something accomplished is finished or completed.

clue.text: Dead German recollected as a fine woman

indicators.note: recollected read as re-collected means gathered up again in a new order

explanation.surface: A dead German is remembered as a fine lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' looks like 'remembered', but it says re-collect the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A grande dame is a dignified, distinguished older lady.

clue.text: Big vessels being manoeuvred into lake, risk regularly taken

indicators.note: manoeuvred means moved about, so the letters of into lake are rearranged
regularly means taking every other letter of risk

explanation.surface: Large ships are steered into a lake, with risks taken now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being manoeuvred' rearranges INTOLAKE to OILTANKE, and 'regularly' takes RS, the first and third letters of 'risk'. 'taken' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil tankers are huge ships that carry crude oil.

clue.text: Final words, perhaps, in girl's service book

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, and the 's adds S
a missal is the book of the Mass

explanation.surface: Closing words are found in a girl's prayer book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Final words' looks like the end of a speech; here it is the dismissal that ends the Mass, 'Ite, missa est'.
explanation.definitionFit: The dismissal is the formula that sends the congregation away at the close of a church service.

clue.text: Level of sound finishes off restricting odd pulsating sounds

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the level of sound encloses the word for odd

parts.note: dB, the decibel, measures sound level
rum is old British slang for odd
to eat is to finish food off, so finishes off means eats

explanation.surface: A sound engineer notes the volume ends up containing strange throbbing noises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricting' applies to the level of sound and the odd word, even though 'finishes off' sits between them in the clue; rum meaning odd is dated British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Drumbeats are the rhythmic thuds made by striking a drum.

clue.text: Mountain height with a character at the top?

parts.note: an alp is a mountain

explanation.surface: A climber reaches a mountain peak to find someone standing on the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' means a letter: alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha heads the Greek alphabet, so it is the letter at the top of the list.

clue.text: Espy a lion unexpectedly in Pacific region

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests a surprise turn, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller sees a lion by surprise somewhere in the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: Polynesia is the large group of islands spread across the central and southern Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Dark one gets left in

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for left inside the word for one

parts.note: a unit is one

explanation.surface: Someone in the dark is the one left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlit means without lights, hence dark.

clue.text: Ultimately the flighty type wants friend for good

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so take the last letter of the

parts.note: a tern is a seabird, literally a flying type
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: In the end the fickle person needs a companion who will stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flighty type' suggests a fickle person; here it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: For good means for ever, permanently.

clue.text: Suppress disorderly leaves around the end of autumn

indicators.note: around means going round the outside, so the rearranged leaves enclose the last letter of autumn
disorderly means messed up, so the letters of leaves are rearranged
the end of means the final letter of autumn

explanation.surface: Someone tries to hold back unruly leaves as autumn closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorderly' turns LEAVES into ESLAVE, and 'around' puts that round N, the last letter of 'autumn' (named by 'the end of').
explanation.definitionFit: To enslave is to subjugate, oppress and hold down.

clue.text: Some damsel destined to be the one who will succeed?

definitions.text: to be the one who will succeed

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale damsel is fated to inherit the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: The eldest child traditionally succeeds to a title, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: By primogeniture the firstborn child is the heir, the person due to take over.

clue.text: Kitchen chemical that could make a sink go bad

indicators.note: could make says these letters can be rearranged to produce the answer

explanation.surface: A household cleaner that might cause a sink to go off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the letters; 'could make' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodium bicarbonate is used in cooking as a raising agent.

clue.text: Colour of driver's accessory, as you might say?

indicators.note: as you might say means as pronounced, so the sound of the driver's accessory counts

parts.note: a car key is the item a driver carries

explanation.surface: What shade is a motorist's accessory, one might ask?
explanation.walkthrough: Said in a non-rhotic British accent, 'car key' sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Khaki is a dull brownish-yellow shade, familiar from army uniforms.

clue.text: Boss — important person, from what we hear

indicators.note: from what we hear means according to the sound, so the word for important person is said

parts.note: a nob is British slang for a wealthy, important person

explanation.surface: A boss is described as a big shot, by rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' is not a manager but a round knob or stud, as on a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a raised round stud, as on a shield or ceiling.

clue.text: Boat pole to get punt finally moving off

parts.note: a bar is a pole

indicators.note: moving off means departing, so the final letter of punt leaves the word get

parts.note: get is taken as written here

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of punt

explanation.surface: On a river a punter uses a pole to push the boat away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving off' takes T, the last letter of 'punt' (named by 'finally'), away from GET to leave GE. 'Boat pole' reads as one phrase but is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A barge is a flat-bottomed boat used on canals and rivers.

clue.text: Healthy wife lacking flaw

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the letter for wife is removed

parts.note: whole means healthy, sound in body

explanation.surface: A fit man without a wife has a weakness.
explanation.definitionFit: A hole is a fault or gap, as in a hole in an argument.

clue.text: Walk as girl going around hobbling

indicators.note: going around means encircling, so the girl's name surrounds the word for hobbling

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name
hobbling means limping, lame

explanation.surface: A girl walks with a limp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walk' is a noun: an alameda is a tree-lined promenade.
explanation.definitionFit: An alameda is a shaded public promenade, a word from Spanish.

clue.text: Type briefly backing boy, inputting power as advocate

indicators.note: backing means supporting from behind, so the shortened type comes after the boy
inputting means putting in, so the abbreviation for power goes inside the word for boy

parts.note: a son is a boy

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the word for type is dropped

parts.note: a sort is a type

explanation.surface: A kind of person briefly supports a lad and supplies power as his champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' clips the final T of the word for type, and 'backing' puts what is left behind the boy holding power.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponsor is a backer who supports and promotes a cause or person.

clue.text: Miss frowning endlessly keeps legs hidden

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the shortened frowning word holds the legs
endlessly means without its last letter

parts.note: stern means frowning, severe
pins is informal for legs

explanation.surface: A severe woman hides her legs from view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' clips the final N of the frowning word, which 'keeps' the legs inside it. 'hidden' just adds to the picture of a modest woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss is the title of an unmarried woman.

clue.text: Money earned in London, say? It goes down the drain

parts.note: London is in the south-east of England, SE
a wage is money earned

explanation.surface: Wages earned in London disappear down the drain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'London, say' gives SE, the south-east region of England, where London lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewage is waste water carried away through drains and sewers.
